top10.why: 'It quoted our old draft as the decision': instant pain; tabs and sockets fix it.
Dead wiki link felt at once; pins make 'what must not change' visible.
'Passed every check, customer found the bug'; lintel icons show checks differ in kind.
'AI sent the email before anyone looked': universal fear; send waits behind a rule gate.
'Perfect on screen, print cut off': everyday miss becomes a new kind of check.
'AI filled our wiki overnight': small batches checked against pins; huge relatability.
'I sent the client's notes': leak felt instantly; sealed card stays at the gate.
'The retry sent the refund twice': money pain; ticks resume, pay happens once.
'Report said green, screen said otherwise': check the thing, not its label.
'We fixed this exact mistake last month': a miss becomes a pin that bounces it.

flags.problem: README's 100% Game of 24 claim, no method shown: overclaim if put on screen.
95.3/93.8/63% for conditions A/B/C that the README never defines; numbers can't be read.
Field benchmarks, not Manu's run; puts 'proof', 'Lean', 'oracle' on screen (RESEARCH §2 caution).
External paper's 11.94% about Lean-verified workflows; risks implying AI routinely makes formal proofs.
'94%' in a caption, not on a card; the figure is from JEV-works, but the board sources it to jev score_fill. Source mismatch.
'0.82–0.91' in a caption, off-card (N8); also a unit the viewer can't feel.
'Citation audit 47 of 60' is borrowed from Memory graph map, not from OmniMemory/kraken.
Same 47-of-60 citation audit borrowed into a stalks-and-sections board; wrong source.
'proven' / 'Noether proved' in FELT: jargon in FELT, and it primes the overclaim.
Names Noether and 'proved' in viewer words; breaks N5 and the §4 caution.
Puts 'Noether's theorem' on screen, even negated; say 'Noether-inspired' only.
'It proved itself' says 'prove' about a gate (RESEARCH §2); rephrase to 'It caught it twice'.
'once it proves itself': the same 'prove' wording problem.
Planned explainer, not a run; 'one equation makes them consistent' has to be labelled Illustration, not evidence.
The 19.7% is second-hand through a README; verify USENIX 2025 primary before it goes on screen.
